structure_chosen: Flat foundation layer + one-service-per-entity, tied by a facade and a manifest. taskly/ holds single-responsibility foundation modules where each cross-cutting concern has exactly one home: ids.py (base62 + short ref codes), validation.py (all input rules), security.py (hashing + tokens), dates.py (timestamps/formatting), pagination.py (the list envelope), models.py (dataclasses + the one serializer to_dict), store.py (persistence + get_or_404), errors.py (error taxonomy). taskly/services/ holds one module per domain entity (users, projects, tasks, tags, comments, notifications), each depending only on foundation modules and on lower services injected via constructor (tasks->tags+notifications, comments->notifications). taskly/api.py is the Taskly facade that wires the store and all services in dependency order and exposes them as attributes (app.users, app.tasks, ...). MANIFEST.md at the root is a capability->file table so an agent can jump straight to the owning file for any rule change. A smoke_test.py exercises every capability end to end and passes. Chose this over a single mega-module (would force reading unrelated code and invite copy-paste) and over deep layering like models/repositories/services/controllers per entity (too many near-empty files to hop through for a small API).
self_audit_duplication: list/search boilerplate is repeated across 6 service methods: [filter comprehension] -> items.sort(key=lambda x: x.created_at) -> paginate([to_dict(x) for x in items], page, per_page). The paginate ENVELOPE is centralized, but this 3-line materialize-sort-paginate shape is copy-pasted. A single helper like paginate_query(items, sort_key, page, per_page) that maps to_dict internally would collapse all six to one line each. I did not extract it and that is real duplication.
The 'validate_str(description or "", ...)' idiom for optional trimmed strings appears in projects.create and tasks.create; a validate_optional_str helper would dedupe it.
The 'sort by created_at' lambda is written out in every list method (six copies) instead of a shared constant/helper.

get_or_404(store.users, id, 'user') and get_or_404(store.projects, id, 'project') call sites recur across services; this is shared-helper reuse rather than logic duplication, but the existence-check-before-write pattern is still repeated verbatim many times and could be a decorator or small guard helper.
self_audit_missing_cases: No authorization/membership model: any existing user can complete, assign, comment on, or tag ANY task in ANY project. There is no project-membership or ownership check beyond 'the id exists'. login/authenticate work, but nothing consumes the authenticated identity to gate writes.

Sessions never expire: Session.created_at is stored but never checked, yet authenticate() raises AuthError('invalid or EXPIRED session token') — the 'expired' wording is misleading because expiry is not implemented. logout() exists but there is no TTL.
Cannot unassign a task: TaskService.assign requires an assignee_id and runs get_or_404 on it, so passing None to clear the assignee raises NotFoundError instead of unassigning.

Inconsistent not-found semantics on filtered reads: tasks.list/search with a non-existent project_id, and notifications.list with a non-existent user_id, silently return an empty page rather than raising NotFoundError, unlike every write path. tags.list also does not 404 a bad project_id.

created_at has only second granularity, so entities created within the same second are ordered only by dict insertion order (relies on stable sort + insertion-ordered dicts); ties are not broken by id, so ordering is implementation-dependent under bursty creation.
short_code() reference codes are not checked for collisions; two notifications can share a ref_code. Harmless today (ref_code is not a key) but wrong if a lookup-by-ref feature is added later.

No length bound on email input (validate_email checks shape but not max length), and no entity deletion/cascade anywhere, so orphan cleanup is impossible (mitigated only by delete being absent entirely).
Pagination accepts arbitrarily large page numbers (returns empty items with has_next=False) without signaling 'page out of range'; acceptable but not flagged to the caller.
layout_rationale: Optimized for an agent's actual workflow: locate the owning file, edit one place, avoid re-deriving cross-file invariants. (1) One-home-per-concern means a rule change is a single-file edit with zero grep-for-duplicates: email format only in validation.py, id scheme only in ids.py, serialization/sensitive-field stripping only in models.to_dict, lookup/404 only in store.get_or_404. (2) MANIFEST.md is a direct capability->file jump table, so an agent skips exploratory reading. (3) Uniform contracts (services take/return dicts, list+search always return the paginate envelope, missing entities always via get_or_404) make each new service predictable from any existing one — an agent can pattern-match tasks.py to write a new entity service. (4) Explicit, acyclic dependency direction documented in services/__init__ and enforced by constructor injection in api.py means an agent can add or modify a service knowing exactly what it may call. (5) Flat module names (short, greppable, no deep nesting) keep path reasoning cheap for tool-based navigation. (6) smoke_test.py doubles as executable usage documentation and a regression guard an agent can run after any edit.

structure_chosen:
Flat, single-responsibility Python package `taskly/` (16 files) plus a mirrored `tests/` directory (12 files, 169 unittest cases, all passing on stdlib only — no pytest/pip install needed). Layout:

  taskly/
    __init__.py        package map / manifest docstring + public re-exports
    api.py              TasklyAPI facade — the one file that wires services together
    models.py            plain dataclasses (User, Project, Task, TaskStatus, Tag, Comment, Notification) — data only, no logic
    store.py             generic Repository[T] + TasklyStore (all in-memory state lives here)
    errors.py             exception hierarchy (TasklyError -> ValidationError/NotFoundError/AuthError/ConflictError)
    users.py              UserService: create/get user, email validation + password hashing, authenticate, sessions
    projects.py           ProjectService: create/get/list
    tags.py                TagService: get-or-create (deduped by normalized name), list
    tasks.py               TaskService: create/list/complete/assign/add_tags/search
    comments.py             CommentService: add/list, fires notifications
    notifications.py        NotificationService: create/list/mark_read/get_by_reference_code (short base62 codes)
    ids.py                  base62 id + reference-code generation (single source of truth)
    validation.py            shared input validators (email/password/strings/ids)
    dates.py                  UTC datetime formatting/parsing (ISO-8601, human, relative)
    pagination.py             generic Page/paginate()/validate_pagination() used by every list/search method

  tests/  — one test_<module>.py per taskly module, plus test_api_integration.py exercising the full cross-service workflow end to end.

Rule applied throughout: exactly one entity per module, exactly one module allowed to mutate that entity's Repository, and every cross-cutting concern (ids, validation, dates, pagination, errors) factored into its own tiny module so no service reimplements it inline.
self_audit_duplication: The 'sort items, then call paginate()' boilerplate is repeated near-identically in five places (ProjectService.list_projects, TaskService.list_tasks, TaskService.search_tasks, CommentService.list_comments, NotificationService.list_notifications) instead of being factored into one shared `sort_and_paginate(items, key, reverse, limit, offset)` helper in pagination.py. Each call site differs slightly (sort key, direction, filter predicates) so it isn't a copy-paste bug, but it is duplicated shape that a future edit to pagination semantics would need to touch in five files instead of one.

The 'fire a notification if a NotificationService is wired and some precondition holds' pattern is written twice by hand (TaskService._notify_assignment, CommentService._notify_new_comment) with no shared helper, even though both are a 2-line guard + create_notification call.

validate_id() is called at the top of nearly every get_*/list_*/mark_* method as a defensive type check; this is intentional reuse of one function rather than duplicated logic, but it's worth noting the same guard clause is now pasted (as a one-line call) into ~10 methods.
self_audit_missing_cases: Confirmed live bug: TaskService.create_task/add_tags type their tag_names parameter as Iterable[str] but never check it isn't itself a bare str. Since str satisfies Iterable[str], calling create_task(..., tag_names='urgent') silently iterates per character and creates 6 garbage one-letter tags ('u','r','g','e','n','t') instead of one 'urgent' tag — verified by running it. Should reject non-list/tuple/set input or explicitly special-case str.
No way to unassign a task: assign_task() requires a valid, existing assignee_id, so there is no supported path back to assignee_id=None once a task has been assigned.

Task search (search_tasks) only matches title + description text; it does not search by tag name, even though tags exist as a first-class concept — a caller cannot find 'all tasks tagged urgent' via search_tasks.

NotificationService._unique_reference_code() rescans every existing notification (O(n) `{n.reference_code for n in store.notifications.all()}`) on every single notification creation; fine at demo scale, degrades on a long-lived instance with many notifications.

verify_password()'s except branch (malformed/corrupt stored hash) returns False without doing any PBKDF2 work, while the normal wrong-password path does the full computation — a theoretical timing side-channel distinguishing 'corrupt hash' from 'wrong password', not addressed.
Sessions are only evicted lazily on lookup (get_user_by_session), not swept proactively; an idle expired session sits in store.sessions forever if nobody ever tries to use it again.

Email validation is a deliberately simple regex (documented as such) that will accept some invalid addresses (e.g. consecutive dots) and reject a few obscure-but-valid ones — acceptable for this scope but not RFC 5322 complete.
No rate limiting / lockout on authenticate() — unlimited password guesses are possible against a single account.

Notification 'kind' and Task 'status' inconsistently use a plain str vs. a TaskStatus Enum respectively; kind has no closed set of allowed values, so a caller can pass an arbitrary/typo'd kind string that nothing validates against a known vocabulary.
layout_rationale: Optimized for an AI agent's actual navigation pattern: grep-by-entity-name finds exactly one file, and cross-entity edits are easy to reason about because dependency direction is explicit and acyclic (users <- projects/tasks/comments/notifications; tasks/notifications <- comments; nothing imports "up"). The __init__.py doubles as a manifest/map an agent can read first to orient itself without exploring the whole tree, and api.py is kept intentionally thin (pure wiring, no logic) so it stays a trustworthy one-glance answer to "what exists and how is it connected." Each entity's CRUD is owned by exactly one service module and the only file allowed to write that entity's Repository, which is what makes duplicate-logic auditing tractable — a reviewer (or an agent) only has to check one file per entity for business-rule correctness. Shared mechanics (ids, validation, dates, pagination, security, errors) are isolated into single-purpose modules specifically so an agent adding a new entity later reuses them instead of reinventing them inline, and the parallel tests/test_<module>.py naming means "where are this file's tests" never requires searching.

structure_chosen: Taskly API organized into 8 files with layered architecture: (1) main.py - FastAPI app + HTTP routes; (2) handlers.py - business logic handlers organized by domain (User, Project, Task, Comment, Notification); (3) models.py - Pydantic request/response schemas with field validators; (4) db.py - single Database class managing all in-memory storage with indexed lookups; (5) utils.py - shared utilities (base62 ID generation, password hashing, email validation, date formatting, pagination normalization); (6) manifest.md - comprehensive navigation guide for AI agents; (7) requirements.txt - dependencies; (8) AUDIT.md - edge cases and bugs identified. Dependencies flow: main→handlers→(db+utils), handlers→models, models→utils. No circular imports.
self_audit_duplication: Email validation: Pydantic EmailStr validator + utils.validate_email_address() both normalize (harmless redundancy)
Authorization checks: Repeated pattern 'if project.user_id != user_id: raise 403' across handlers (necessary consistency, not code duplication)
Response model construction: TaskResponse/ProjectResponse/etc created multiple times in handlers (required for type conversion, unavoidable)
No utility function duplication: All validation, hashing, ID generation, date formatting centralized in utils.py
No database operation duplication: All CRUD patterns centralized in db.py Database class
No route duplication: Each endpoint defined once in main.py
self_audit_missing_cases: CRITICAL: Task completion notification never fires in update_task() - checks task['completed'] AFTER update, always False (handlers.py:270)
MEDIUM: Duplicate notifications if complete_task() called multiple times (handlers.py:283-306)
MEDIUM: Search pagination contract violated - filters results after db returns limit, may return fewer items than requested (handlers.py:309-328)
MEDIUM: datetime.utcnow() deprecated in Python 3.12+, use datetime.now(timezone.utc) instead (utils.py:127)
MEDIUM: GET /users/{user_id} lacks authentication, allows user discovery (main.py:84-87)
LOW: Empty string validation edge case - descriptions of only whitespace become empty after strip() (models.py:59,89)
LOW: No validation that assigned_to user exists in project (potential open collaboration model)
LOW: No authorization check for comment creation - any user can comment on any task
LOW: No soft deletes - tasks/projects permanent
LOW: Search crosses all projects, then filters by authorization in handler (inefficient)
EDGE CASE: Self-notifications possible when user comments on their own task
EDGE CASE: Invalid user/task/project IDs not validated before database lookup
EDGE CASE: No concurrency control (race conditions in simultaneous requests)
EDGE CASE: No rate limiting or DoS protection
layout_rationale: This structure optimizes for AI agent maintenance/extension: (1) Zero utility duplication means utilities.py is the single source of truth for validation/hashing/IDs - agents need only check one file to understand validation logic. (2) Single db.py Database class with clear index management enables agents to understand data flow without tracing through multiple files. (3) Handler classes organize business logic by domain with consistent patterns (create/get/list/update) making new endpoints predictable to add. (4) manifest.md provides detailed navigation with file purposes, class methods, indexes, and extension points - agents read this first to understand architecture. (5) Dependency graph is linear (main→handlers→db/utils) with no circular imports, preventing agent confusion. (6) Separation of concerns (routing, business logic, data, validation) means changing one concern doesn't require touching others. (7) Models.py schemas are centralized, so adding a new field requires touching one place. (8) All 1864 lines across 8 files keep codebase small enough for agents to hold entire context while reading files, yet organized enough to avoid overwhelming single files. No file exceeds 450 lines. This structure sacrifices some human-convenience-oriented groupings (like putting all auth in one module) for AI-agent-convenience (clear separation enabling targeted reads and modifications).
